summary: Earth Information Jukebox transforms real NASA Earth observations into an interactive 16-bit eco-adventure game, a climate simulator, and a musical data experience. Players explore five distinct environmental zones, solving puzzles and answering challenges using real satellite data from the in-game "map" field guide. Completing all five missions unlocks an interactive climate simulator where users can adjust co2, methane, oxygen, and temperature to visualize their impact on climate, sea levels, ice, forests, coral reefs, and biodiversity from 1750 to 2100. Alongside the game, a built in jukebox converts five real NASA datasets (ECCO2, GEDI, SMAP, GISTEMP, and PACE) into music. Designed to make satellite science intuitive and playful for students and the public, the entire experience is built with full accessibility featuring keyboard controls, ARIA labels, and optional voice-over narration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Eco-Quest: a 16-bit game with 5 missions. Each one has a puzzle, a question based on NASA data, and a companion (Willow) who shares NASA facts.

Simulator (unlocked after the missions): sliders for CO₂, CH₄, O₂ and temperature, with explanations of immediate effects, long-term effects and the science. A replay (1750–2100) compares "no intervention" (700 ppm CO₂) with "intervention" (360 ppm).

NASA Jukebox: 5 tracks where real data becomes sound (ECCO2 ocean currents, GEDI forest canopy, SMAP soil moisture, GISTEMP climate, PACE ocean color).

WHY THE PROJECT IS CREATIVE:

project turns real NASA satellite data into a playful 16-bit adventure where you explore five zones and crack puzzles to save the planet. Beating the game unlocks a hands-on climate simulator where you can experiment with Earth's future from 1750 to 2100 in real time. Best of all, a built-in jukebox remixes live space observations into music, making real science something you can genuinely play and groove to.

WHY IT MATTERS

Satellite data is powerful but abstract. Playing and listening to it helps people understand how Earth systems connect and how human choices change them.

NASA DATA

NASA Earth Information Center, ECCO2, GEDI, SMAP, GISTEMP v4, PACE, OCO-2/OCO-3, NASA SVS.

BUILT WITH

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file: Canvas (globe and game), Web Audio API (music and sonification), speech synthesis (voice-over).

ACCESSIBILITY

Keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, reduced-motion support, and toggles for sound, music and voice.

what factor did the team consider:

Our team focused on balancing scientific accuracy with accessibility and fun. We considered how to make complex NASA satellite datasets intuitive for students and the general public, which led us to combine a nostalgic 16-bit adventure, an in-game field guide, and music sonification. Finally, we prioritized inclusive design—ensuring anyone could explore the data through keyboard controls, ARIA labels, and optional voice-over narration
